threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' instead of the 'Ginger Line'. That's a surefire sign you haven't been around long.
Caught a glimpse of an old bloke serenading a pigeon on the N36 last night. Only in Peckham would that feel normal at 3 AM.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted an artist painting a mural while a couple argued in Turkish over a spilled kebab in front of my local Späti.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find U-Bahn trains adorned with art installations, but only in Friedrichshain does it feel like walking through a gallery on your way to work.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local will turn their face away when they see a Muni bus approaching, knowing it’s just going to be another 15-minute wait.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni with a passenger serenading us; loud enough to drown out the usual grit, but not the smell of the street. Classic SF vibe.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just stroll into any bar and get a proper vermut. Little do they know, the locals have their favorites and they won’t share.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still refer to the metro stops by the old names, like 'Reforma' instead of 'L3'. That and a tendency to use the bus instead of walking.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'shopping trolley' instead of a 'trolley' like everyone else—real locals know how to shorten that chat.
Caught a guy at Brixton bus stop talking to himself about the 'ghosts' on the 35. Said he'd seen them twice this week, both times after midnight.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The way the kebab shop owner knows my order before I even step in—now that's when it hit me. This is home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You know that feeling when the U-Bahn stops for a minute just because? It's like the city's taking a moment to breathe, and you're right there with it.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they instantly pull out their phone to check BART delays the moment they hear anything resembling a loud bang.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday a guy on the bus serenaded us with a ukulele while we were stuck behind a broken streetcar. The delays add character, I guess.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about the squares and bars, but they miss the quiet siestas that wrap the streets in a soft lull.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their shoes—sporty sneakers and flip-flops are a dead giveaway. Locals stick to sturdy flats or loafers for the cobbles.
